- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days), suggesting a persistent upward bias.
- After sharp price spikes, model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect, creating a lagged downward bias in subsequent days.
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged downward trends, failing to capture mean reversion or support levels.
- Forecasts show poor sensitivity to recent low-price periods; model often ignores recent dips and fails to adjust downward.
- Model exhibits strong persistence in high forecasts, even when true prices are declining — suggesting lack of momentum decay modeling.
- In cases of strong upward momentum, model overreacts and forecasts higher than true price, especially in the first 7–10 days.
- Model underestimates prices during transition zones (e.g., after a spike or before a dip), often missing the “mean-reversion” phase.
- Forecasts tend to be overly optimistic in the short term (1–3 days) and overly pessimistic in the medium term (5–10 days), indicating horizon mismatch.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonal or calendar-driven price patterns (e.g., end-of-month or quarter-end volatility).
- Model overfits to recent high prices, leading to persistent overestimation even when true prices are falling.
